4 findings carried by reviewers against `content/blog/glm-5-3-license-revenue-gate.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Say that the LICENSE file is bilingual, not English-only

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260902-22-carry-1.md`.

The post tells the reader what is in the file: "The rest of the file is clause 1 (the MIT-style grant, the notice condition, and a requirement that use comply with applicable laws), clause 3 (a standard as-is warranty), and a contact address, glmlicense@z.ai." Fetched from https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3/raw/main/LICENSE on 2026-09-02 (4263 bytes), the file does not end there: after a `-----` separator it carries a complete Chinese version of the same licence, and the review-gate sentence appears there as "安全审查的范围和方式由Z.AI合理确定" (合理 = reasonably). The two halves agree on substance, and the file names no governing language, which for a licence is worth a clause of its own. One sentence added to that enumeration — that the English text is followed by a Chinese translation of the whole licence, with no governing-language clause — would close the gap between what the post says the file contains and what a reader who opens the raw URL will find. Two smaller notes in the same sentence: the MIT-style grant is actually the preamble paragraph above clause 1, not part of clause 1, and "The review itself is two sentences of the file and nothing more" is true of the English half only.

### "$10B or more" and "trailing 12 months" both loosen the licence's own words

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260902-23-carry-1.md`.

The rewritten sentence keeps "your group's revenue over any trailing 12 months is $10B or more". The fetched LICENSE says "exceeds 10 billion US dollars (or the equivalent in other currencies) in total over any consecutive 12 months". Two slips in one clause: "or more" includes a group at exactly $10.0B, which "exceeds" does not, and "trailing" narrows the window to one ending now, where "any consecutive" reaches any 12-month span. The post's own analysis section gets the window right ("over any consecutive 12 months, so a fiscal year is the wrong window to check against"), and the title and lede get the threshold right ("above $10B", "passes $10B"), so this is the one place the closing summary drifts from the quoted text. "over any consecutive 12 months is above $10B" fixes both.

### The MIT-style grant is the unnumbered preamble, not part of clause 1

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260902-23-carry-2.md`.

The post says "The rest of the file is clause 1 (the MIT-style grant, the notice condition, and a requirement that use comply with applicable laws)". In the LICENSE fetched 2026-09-02 the grant is the unnumbered paragraph above the numbered list — it opens "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person or entity (the Licensee) obtaining a copy of this software" and closes "subject to the following conditions:" — and clause 1 is exactly two sentences, the notice condition and the applicable-laws sentence, with no grant language in it. The post's argument in "The condition attaches to all commercial use, not just MaaS" leans on the grant being made subject to the conditions, which is a preamble fact, so naming it correctly strengthens that section. This was raised in the pass-1 record for j-20260902-20 and was not transcribed into `data/carried/`, so it is currently tracked nowhere; I re-verified it against the file myself rather than taking that record's word for it.

### The licence file is bilingual and names no governing language

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260902-23-carry-3.md`.

"The rest of the file is clause 1 ..., clause 3 ..., and a contact address" describes 14 of the file's 29 lines. Below a `-----` rule the same three clauses appear in full Chinese translation (100亿美元 for the ten-billion line, 任意连续12个月 for the window, 由Z.AI合理确定 for "reasonably determined by Z.AI"), and nothing in either half says which language governs. For a post whose whole subject is the exact reach of one clause, an unremarked parallel text with no governing-language clause is a real fact about the instrument. One sentence in "Clause 2, verbatim" would close it. Also raised in the pass-1 record for j-20260902-20 and likewise not transcribed anywhere.

### Restore the "with the right tools and access" qualifier on the capability sentence

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-05-carry-1.md`.

The post's second paragraph reads: 'The threshold, in OpenAI's words, means Astra can "find previously unknown security flaws and develop ways to exploit them across many well-protected systems without a person guiding each step"'. The page's sentence is 'We now believe Astra meets the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under our Preparedness Framework, meaning that with the right tools and access, it can find previously unknown security flaws and develop ways to exploit them across many well-protected systems without a person guiding each step.' The quote itself is exact, but the conditional clause "with the right tools and access" is dropped, and dropping it strengthens the claim in the direction the rest of the post is careful about. Fix: extend the quotation to start at "with the right tools and access".

### Drop or qualify "independently" in the SecurityWeek sentence

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-05-carry-2.md`.

The post says 'SecurityWeek's coverage, published 2 September, carries the 91.5% and 59% pair independently.' SecurityWeek's line — verified by fetching it, 2026-09-03 — is "Astra now declines 91.5% of cyber-related jailbreak attempts in its testing, up from 59% for its predecessor, GPT-5.6 Sol", which restates OpenAI's own figures rather than measuring them. "Independently" invites a reader to hear independent corroboration of numbers the post elsewhere correctly calls OpenAI's word. Fix: "carries the same 91.5% and 59% pair" and delete "independently".

3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/blog/thomson-reuters-thomson-model.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Note the base-model columns when citing this post's benchmark reading

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-02-carry-1.md`.

The post writes "Its benchmark table averages 74.6 across the board, against 71.2 for Gemma 4-31B and 68.2 for Haiku 4.5" and cites only the two competitor columns. The same table I fetched from the model card also carries Snowdon-1.1-Small at 71.7 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 71.7 — so the $40M bought +2.9 points over the free Apache-2.0 base. Sharper still, on the row the post does quote, Thomson's Stanford LegalBench 79.9 is BELOW its own base (Qwen 80.3, Snowdon 80.9), and on MBE Bar Exam 83.4 barely clears Snowdon's 83.1. Nothing in the post is false — it never claims Thomson beats its base — but the base columns are the strongest available evidence against the parity story and they are left on the table. A future post or wiki fact on Thomson-1.0-Small should carry them.

### Qualify the Hugging Face download figures as 30-day counts

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-02-carry-2.md`.

The post says bartowski's GGUF "had 70,172 downloads by 3 September against 1,130 for the source repo". Both figures are exact — I re-fetched them and got 70172 and 1130 — but the HF API's `downloads` field is a rolling 30-day count, not a cumulative total, and "by 3 September" reads as cumulative. It happens not to matter here (thomsonreuters/ Thomson-1.0-Small was created 2026-08-18, so the 30-day window covers the repo's whole life), but the qualifier is dropped and the same phrasing would be wrong on an older repo. Related: the Sources bullet names "Hugging Face API records for Thomson-1.0-Small, Snowdon1.1-Small, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and bartowski's GGUF conversion" while linking only the first endpoint.

### Name the post, not the internal job id, in the Thomson annotation

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-06-carry-1.md`.

The annotation ends "the correction in prose is the post on this site j-20260903-02". That string renders verbatim to visitors — escaped plain text in the home page's change rail (lib/render/home.mjs) and inside the changes RSS item body (lib/feeds.mjs) — where a loop job id is meaningless and unclickable. It is correct (ledger.jsonl line 72 records j-20260903-02 as the post job, outcome done, review1 approve, and its post is content/blog/thomson-reuters-thomson-model.md, whose covers: anchor declares this same change key). Naming the post by title or by /blog/ slug instead of by job id would let a reader actually reach it.

3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/model/anthropic-claude-opus-4-7-fast.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Transclude the live standard-row price instead of restating it

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-01-carry-1.md`.

The sentence reads "its last-known values as of 2026-09-01, 0.00003 in / 0.00015 out per token against the standard row's 0.000005 / 0.000025". The first pair is a dated historical value and correctly a literal — the row is gone and cannot be transcluded. The second pair is not: anthropic/claude-opus-4.7 is live ($vanished false, $as_of 2026-09-03) and model/anthropic-claude-opus-4-7 already declares price_input and price_output as feed facts, so those two numbers can rot in prose exactly as specs/wiki forbids, taking "six times the base" with them. The reading that "as of 2026-09-01" scopes both pairs is available and is why this is not a revise, but the fix is one edit — {{fact:model/anthropic-claude-opus-4-7#price_input}} and #price_output in place of the two literals.

### Re-wrap the reflowed line in the third paragraph

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-01-carry-2.md`.

The edit left one line unwrapped: "capabilities with higher output speed at premium 6x pricing." Nothing in either source records how those" runs to about 100 characters where every other line in the file wraps near 72. Cosmetic, source-only, no render effect — re-wrap the paragraph.

### Record the two vanished-row price literals as deliberate, so the new currency-literal warnings are not later read as rot

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-13-carry-1.md`.

This diff adds eight `currency-literal` build warnings that did not exist before — measured with lib/currency.mjs's own findCurrencyLiterals against df9751b~1 and df9751b: content/wiki/model/anthropic-claude-opus-4-7-fast.md goes 6 -> 10 hits (new: price:$30.00, price:$150.00, price:$5.00, price:$25.00) and content/wiki/model/nvidia-nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b-batch.md goes 0 -> 4 (price:$0.625, price:$0.60, price:$3.125, price:$2.40). Each warning reads "state it with a transclusion, {{fact:<kind>/<slug>#<field>}}, so it stays current" — advice that is impossible to follow here, because the rows are gone: data/derived/feed-rows.json holds `"anthropic/claude-opus-4.7-fast": {"$as_of": null, "$status": null, "$vanished": true}` with no pricing key to bind to. The warnings are therefore correct-by-construction noise on every future build, and nothing in the tree says so. The corpus already has the shape for this — three standing ledgers (data/price-attribution-debt.json, arxiv-pin-debt.json, snapshot-census-debt.json) exist precisely so a permanent warning is not mistaken for an unfixed defect. A one-line note in either of those files' style, or an HTML comment on each page naming the vanished row, would fix it. Not blocking: the check is a warning by design and its own header anticipates exactly this case ("a build that failed on this would break every historical rebuild the moment a quoted price appeared in a legitimate sentence").

### Trim the duplicated wording out of the output-tokens fact value

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-11-carry-1.md`.

output_tokens_per_task carries value "~48k at high reasoning (a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task)", and both prose sentences that transclude it already supply that framing themselves. The model entry reads "average output tokens per task rose to {{fact:... #output_tokens_per_task}}, lifting cost per task to {{fact:... #cost_per_task}} at high reasoning", so it renders as "average output tokens per task rose to ~48k at high reasoning (a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task), lifting cost per task to ~$0.58 at high reasoning" — "average output tokens per task" twice, "at high reasoning" twice. content/wiki/org/google-deepmind.md has the same doubling in its "llm-releases prices that sentence" paragraph. Shortening the value to "~48k" fixes both surfaces at once and loses nothing, since the ~30% and the effort level are already in the sentences. Separately, the source attaches "at high reasoning" to the cost-per-task clause, not to the token count — "a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task (to ~48k) lifts cost per task to ~$0.58 at high reasoning" — so dropping it from this value is also the more faithful reading.

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-11-carry-2.md`.

The model entry's benchmark sentence ends "...Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark at {{fact:...#harveys_legal_agent_benchmark}}, and on {{fact:...#deepswe_v1_1}}." items.detail:
The revised sentence reads "But this model's batch page … still knows the batch variant, but lists no providers and no pricing under it and no deprecation notice anywhere on the page". Two small defects, both introduced by the revision. First, "but … but" in one sentence, and "lists … no deprecation notice anywhere on the page" — the verb "lists" cannot govern that clause, and "anywhere on the page" contradicts the "under it" scope it is coordinated with. Second, the precision is now available to do better: I parsed the live page's `variantGroups` and it contains exactly two groups, `free` (1 endpoint) and `standard` (4 endpoints) — there is no `batch` group at all, empty or otherwise, so "lists no providers and no pricing under it" is true but understates what was measured. Suggested replacement: "still identifies itself as the batch variant — the slug, the heading and its uptime queries all name it — but its variant list now holds only the free and standard groups, with no batch group and so no providers or pricing at all; nothing anywhere on the page announces a deprecation."

items.detail:
The gemini-3-8-flash docket attributes two things to https://9to5google.com/2026/09/02/gemini-3-8-flash-launch/ that I could not reproduce from that page with my own extractor: Wiz's "+7.5-9.7% recall" (the page as I retrieved it says only "higher recall on their internal penetration testing benchmark for a 2.3-5.2x lower cost", with no percentage range), and the sentence "At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels" (I retrieved the adjacent "works harder" framing as "exhibit[s] greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively"). This is NOT a finding that either is wrong — WebFetch's extractor denies text that is present as readily as it invents text, so absence through it proves nothing, and every other figure in this docket reproduced exactly. It is a flag that these two are the only unconfirmed items in the set: the entry job that picks this candidate up should quote whichever sentence the page actually carries, and drop the percentage range if it is not there rather than carry it forward on the docket's authority.
